label: Digital Fundamentals
description: Number systems, Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational building blocks (mux, decoder, adder), simplification, timing basics.

label: Sequential Logic
description: Latches and flip-flops, registers, counters, shift registers, synchronous vs asynchronous reset, setup and hold, clock domains.

label: FSMs
description: Moore and Mealy machines, state encoding, sequence detectors, state minimization, FSM coding style in HDL, common FSM bugs.

label: Relevant Programming
description: HDL basics (Verilog or SystemVerilog), blocking vs non-blocking, testbench structure, plus Python or C as used in hardware workflows.

label: Reasoning
description: Problem decomposition, estimation, trade-off reasoning, risk and failure-mode awareness, debugging methodology.

label: Projects & Behavioral
description: Explaining a project end to end, ownership, teamwork, learning from mistakes, structured communication.

label: Boolean Algebra and Simplification
description: Boolean identities, De Morgan, sum-of-products and product-of-sums forms, Karnaugh maps with don't-cares, proving two expressions equivalent.

proficiency_rubric.1: Recognizes AND, OR, NOT and can evaluate an expression for given inputs.
proficiency_rubric.2: Applies basic identities and De Morgan to simplify a two- or three-variable expression.
proficiency_rubric.3: Minimizes a four-variable function with a Karnaugh map, uses don't-cares correctly, and verifies the result.
proficiency_rubric.4: Chooses between SOP and POS for a reason, spots hazards introduced by minimization, and proves equivalence of two forms.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about minimization trade-offs across multi-output logic and explains what a synthesis tool will and will not do for you.

label: Truth Tables and Logic Functions
description: Translating a word specification into a complete truth table and into a logic function, and back; parity, majority, comparison.

proficiency_rubric.1: Fills in a truth table for a single gate.
proficiency_rubric.2: Builds the full table for a three-input word specification and writes a correct expression from it.
proficiency_rubric.3: Handles four or more inputs systematically, identifies don't-care conditions from the specification, and checks the table against corner inputs.
proficiency_rubric.4: Spots an ambiguous specification and resolves it explicitly; recognizes standard functions (parity, majority, one-hot) and their properties.
proficiency_rubric.5: Decomposes a wide function into reusable sub-functions and argues why the decomposition is complete.

label: Number Systems and Two's Complement
description: Binary, hexadecimal, unsigned and two's complement ranges, sign extension, fixed-width wraparound.

proficiency_rubric.1: Converts small numbers between binary, decimal and hexadecimal.
proficiency_rubric.2: States the range of an N-bit unsigned and two's complement number and negates a value.
proficiency_rubric.3: Sign-extends and truncates correctly and predicts wraparound in fixed-width arithmetic.
proficiency_rubric.4: Chooses widths for an arithmetic datapath so no intermediate result overflows, and justifies each width.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about fixed-point formats, rounding and saturation policies and their cost in hardware.

label: Binary Arithmetic and Overflow
description: Half and full adders, ripple carry, carry versus signed overflow, subtraction, saturating arithmetic.

proficiency_rubric.1: Adds two small binary numbers by hand.
proficiency_rubric.2: Builds a full adder from gates and chains them into a ripple-carry adder.
proficiency_rubric.3: Distinguishes carry-out from signed overflow and gives the detection logic for each.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs saturating or wrapping arithmetic to a specification and reasons about the critical path of the adder.
proficiency_rubric.5: Compares adder architectures (ripple, carry-lookahead, carry-select) on delay and area and picks one for a stated constraint.

label: NAND/NOR-only Implementation
description: Building any function from a single gate type, bubble pushing, gate counts.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows that NAND and NOR are universal.
proficiency_rubric.2: Builds NOT, AND and OR from NAND gates only.
proficiency_rubric.3: Converts a sum-of-products expression to a NAND-NAND network using bubble pushing.
proficiency_rubric.4: Minimizes the gate count of a NAND-only implementation and explains where sharing is possible.
proficiency_rubric.5: Relates single-gate-type implementation to CMOS cell cost and explains why libraries favor inverting gates.

label: Multiplexers, Decoders and Encoders
description: Mux, demux, decoder, encoder, priority encoder, comparators; composing larger blocks from smaller ones; implementing functions with a mux.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes what a multiplexer and a decoder do.
proficiency_rubric.2: Writes the expression for a 2:1 and 4:1 mux and a 2-to-4 decoder with enable.
proficiency_rubric.3: Builds an 8:1 mux from smaller muxes, implements a function with a mux, and designs a priority encoder with a valid flag.
proficiency_rubric.4: Handles enables, invalid inputs and priority rules explicitly and compares tree and flat structures on delay.
proficiency_rubric.5: Designs wide selection and arbitration logic under timing constraints and explains the fan-in and fan-out consequences.

label: Latches and Flip-Flops
description: Level-sensitive latch versus edge-triggered flip-flop, transparency, enable, where each is used and why unintended latches are a problem.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows that a flip-flop stores one bit and updates on a clock edge.
proficiency_rubric.2: Explains level-sensitive versus edge-triggered behavior and draws the output for a simple waveform.
proficiency_rubric.3: Traces a small circuit with enables over several cycles and explains why a transparent latch complicates timing.
proficiency_rubric.4: Explains master-slave construction, where latches are used on purpose, and how latch-based timing borrows time.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about metastability at the storage element level and about latch versus flip-flop choices in a real design flow.

label: Registers and Shift Registers
description: Registers with load and enable, serial and parallel shift registers, control priority, serial-to-parallel conversion.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes a register as a group of flip-flops sharing a clock.
proficiency_rubric.2: Designs a register with load enable and a simple serial shift register.
proficiency_rubric.3: Resolves control priority (reset, load, shift, hold) explicitly and traces the contents over several cycles.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs serial-to-parallel and parallel-to-serial conversion with framing and explains bit-order pitfalls.
proficiency_rubric.5: Uses shift structures for LFSRs, CRC or delay lines and reasons about their properties.

label: Counters
description: Synchronous counters, modulo-N, enable and reset priority, recovery from invalid states, terminal count.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes a binary counter and how many flip-flops a given range needs.
proficiency_rubric.2: Designs a synchronous up counter with enable and reset.
proficiency_rubric.3: Designs a modulo-N counter with explicit priority between reset, enable and wrap, and traces it correctly.
proficiency_rubric.4: Handles invalid-state recovery, terminal-count outputs and cascading, and explains glitch risks on decoded outputs.
proficiency_rubric.5: Chooses the counter style (binary, Gray, one-hot, LFSR) for a stated constraint and justifies the choice.

label: Reset Strategies
description: Synchronous versus asynchronous reset, assertion and release, reset synchronizers, what must and need not be reset.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows a reset puts the circuit in a known state.
proficiency_rubric.2: Describes the difference between synchronous and asynchronous reset.
proficiency_rubric.3: Explains the advantages and costs of each and the problem with releasing an asynchronous reset near a clock edge.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs asynchronous-assert, synchronous-release reset and decides which registers need a reset at all.
proficiency_rubric.5: Plans reset across multiple clock domains and power states and reasons about reset-tree timing.

label: Synchronous Edge Detection and Pulses
description: Detecting a rising or falling edge of a sampled signal with a delayed copy, producing a one-cycle pulse, behavior at reset.

proficiency_rubric.1: Understands that a sampled signal only changes at clock edges.
proficiency_rubric.2: Builds a rising-edge detector from one flip-flop and a gate.
proficiency_rubric.3: Draws the cycle-accurate waveform, including the first cycle after reset, and explains the one-cycle latency.
proficiency_rubric.4: Handles asynchronous inputs by synchronizing first and explains what pulse widths can be missed.
proficiency_rubric.5: Designs pulse stretching and toggle-based schemes and reasons about their guarantees.

label: Setup, Hold and Maximum Frequency
description: Setup and hold constraints, clock-to-Q, propagation and contamination delay, skew, computing the minimum clock period, fixing violations.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows data must be stable around the clock edge.
proficiency_rubric.2: States the setup and hold inequalities and identifies the terms in a simple path.
proficiency_rubric.3: Computes the minimum period and checks hold for a given path, including clock skew with the correct sign.
proficiency_rubric.4: Explains why hold violations cannot be fixed by slowing the clock and proposes fixes for both setup and hold violations.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about multi-cycle and false paths, jitter and on-chip variation in a timing sign-off context.

label: Clock Domain Crossing
description: Metastability, two-flop synchronizers, MTBF, crossing a pulse or a bus safely, handshakes and asynchronous FIFOs.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows that signals between unrelated clocks are a problem.
proficiency_rubric.2: Explains metastability and what a two-flop synchronizer does.
proficiency_rubric.3: Explains why a short pulse or a multi-bit bus cannot simply be synchronized bit by bit, and offers a fix for each.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs a handshake or toggle-based pulse crossing and explains the role of Gray code in asynchronous FIFO pointers.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons quantitatively about MTBF and reviews a CDC scheme for reconvergence and reset-crossing problems.

label: Moore and Mealy Machines
description: Where the output depends on state only versus state and input; state count, output timing, glitch sensitivity; converting between the two.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows an FSM has states, transitions and outputs.
proficiency_rubric.2: States the defining difference between Moore and Mealy outputs.
proficiency_rubric.3: Compares the two on state count and on which cycle the output appears, with a concrete example.
proficiency_rubric.4: Converts a machine from one style to the other and explains input-glitch sensitivity and registered outputs.
proficiency_rubric.5: Chooses the style for an interface with timing requirements and defends the choice against alternatives.

label: State Diagrams and Transition Tables
description: Turning a word specification into named states with a meaning, a complete transition and output table, and a checked trace.

proficiency_rubric.1: Reads a given state diagram and follows it for an input sequence.
proficiency_rubric.2: Draws a small state diagram from a word specification.
proficiency_rubric.3: Gives every state a meaning, covers every state and input combination, and validates the table with a trace.
proficiency_rubric.4: Finds unreachable or equivalent states, handles reset and illegal states, and documents assumptions about input sampling.
proficiency_rubric.5: Structures large control logic as cooperating machines and argues completeness and absence of deadlock.

label: Sequence Detectors
description: Detecting a bit pattern in a serial stream, overlapping versus non-overlapping detection, fallback transitions on a mismatch.

proficiency_rubric.1: Understands the task of recognizing a pattern in a bit stream.
proficiency_rubric.2: Designs a detector for a short pattern without overlap.
proficiency_rubric.3: Handles overlap correctly by falling back to the longest suffix that is also a prefix, and proves it with a trace.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs detectors with extra constraints (error tolerance, multiple patterns) and compares Moore and Mealy versions.
proficiency_rubric.5: Generalizes to arbitrary patterns (failure-function construction) and reasons about state minimality.

label: Control FSMs and Handshakes
description: Controllers for request and acknowledge, valid and ready, dispensers and sequencers; level versus edge sensitivity of control inputs.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes a controller as an FSM that sequences actions.
proficiency_rubric.2: Designs a three- or four-state controller from a clear specification.
proficiency_rubric.3: Defines outputs per state, ignores inputs outside the states where they matter, and explains behavior when an input is held.
proficiency_rubric.4: Designs valid and ready or request and acknowledge handshakes without losing or duplicating a transfer.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about deadlock, back-pressure and fairness across interacting controllers.

label: State Encoding
description: Binary, Gray and one-hot encodings; their cost in flip-flops, next-state logic, speed and glitch behavior; safe recovery from illegal states.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows states are stored as bit patterns.
proficiency_rubric.2: Counts the flip-flops needed for binary and for one-hot encoding.
proficiency_rubric.3: Compares binary, Gray and one-hot on area, speed and decoding glitches.
proficiency_rubric.4: Chooses an encoding for an FPGA or ASIC target and handles illegal states safely.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reasons about encoding for low power and fault tolerance and about what synthesis re-encoding does.

label: Blocking and Non-blocking Assignments
description: Verilog scheduling of blocking and non-blocking assignments, which to use where, tracing a clocked block, simulation and synthesis mismatch.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows Verilog has two assignment operators.
proficiency_rubric.2: States the rule: non-blocking in clocked blocks, blocking in combinational blocks.
proficiency_rubric.3: Traces a clocked block with non-blocking assignments over several cycles and explains why a swap works.
proficiency_rubric.4: Explains the race that blocking assignments in clocked blocks create and how simulation can disagree with hardware.
proficiency_rubric.5: Explains the event regions of the simulator and reviews code for subtle ordering bugs.

label: Combinational HDL and Unintended Latches
description: Writing combinational logic in HDL, complete assignment in every branch, default values, sensitivity lists, priority versus parallel case.

proficiency_rubric.1: Writes a simple assign statement.
proficiency_rubric.2: Writes combinational logic in an always block with if or case.
proficiency_rubric.3: Finds an unintended latch caused by an incomplete assignment and fixes it with a default.
proficiency_rubric.4: Reasons about priority versus parallel decoding and what hardware each coding style produces.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reviews combinational code for synthesis quality, X-propagation and lint issues.

label: Sequential HDL Coding
description: Clocked always blocks, reset style in code, enables, coding counters, registers and FSMs in the two-process style.

proficiency_rubric.1: Reads a clocked always block and says what it stores.
proficiency_rubric.2: Codes a register with reset and enable.
proficiency_rubric.3: Codes a counter or an FSM with separated next-state and state-register logic and correct reset.
proficiency_rubric.4: Writes parameterized, lint-clean sequential code and explains what each construct synthesizes to.
proficiency_rubric.5: Designs coding guidelines for a team and reviews code for clocking, reset and CDC hazards.

label: Testbench Basics
description: Clock and reset generation, applying stimulus, checking outputs, self-checking testbenches, choosing test cases.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows a testbench drives a design in simulation.
proficiency_rubric.2: Writes a clock, a reset and a few directed stimulus vectors.
proficiency_rubric.3: Makes the testbench self-checking and picks cases that cover boundaries, not only the happy path.
proficiency_rubric.4: Structures stimulus and checking separately and reasons about what has and has not been covered.
proficiency_rubric.5: Plans verification for a block: coverage goals, random stimulus, assertions and sign-off criteria.

label: Bit Manipulation
description: Masks, shifts, setting and clearing bits, extracting fields, counting bits, power-of-two tests, in C or Python.

proficiency_rubric.1: Knows the bitwise operators.
proficiency_rubric.2: Sets, clears and tests a single bit with a mask.
proficiency_rubric.3: Extracts and inserts a multi-bit field and explains the n & (n - 1) idiom with its edge cases.
proficiency_rubric.4: Handles signedness, width and undefined shifts correctly and writes a register-access helper safely.
proficiency_rubric.5: Designs bit-level data layouts and explains the hardware or compiler cost of each operation.

label: Arrays and Search
description: Indexing and bounds, linear and binary search, two-pointer merging, complexity of simple loops.

proficiency_rubric.1: Loops over an array and reads elements.
proficiency_rubric.2: Implements linear search and a simple merge of two lists.
proficiency_rubric.3: Implements binary search with correct boundaries and states time complexity.
proficiency_rubric.4: Handles duplicates, empty input and overflow in index arithmetic, and proves the loop invariant.
proficiency_rubric.5: Chooses data layout and algorithm for a stated size and access pattern.

label: Basic Data Structures
description: Stack, queue, circular buffer, linked list: operations, full and empty conditions, in-place manipulation.

proficiency_rubric.1: Names common data structures and what they are for.
proficiency_rubric.2: Implements push and pop or enqueue and dequeue for a simple case.
proficiency_rubric.3: Implements a fixed-capacity circular queue with correct full and empty detection.
proficiency_rubric.4: Reverses a linked list in place, reasons about ownership and edge cases, and states complexity.
proficiency_rubric.5: Relates software structures to hardware equivalents (FIFO depth, pointers) and their trade-offs.

label: Code Debugging
description: Reading unfamiliar code, locating an off-by-one or boundary error, explaining the failing input and the fix.

proficiency_rubric.1: Reads short code and says roughly what it does.
proficiency_rubric.2: Finds an obvious bug when pointed to the area.
proficiency_rubric.3: Locates a boundary error unaided, gives an input that exposes it, and fixes it without side effects.
proficiency_rubric.4: Explains the root cause class and proposes a test that would have caught it.
proficiency_rubric.5: Debugs across layers with partial information and leaves the code easier to verify.

label: Debugging Methodology
description: Working from a symptom to a root cause: reproduce, narrow down, form and test hypotheses, confirm the fix.

proficiency_rubric.1: Tries changes until something works.
proficiency_rubric.2: Reproduces the problem and looks at the obvious suspects first.
proficiency_rubric.3: Narrows the search systematically (bisecting in time or in the design) and tests one hypothesis at a time.
proficiency_rubric.4: Reasons from waveforms or logs to a root cause, separates cause from symptom, and verifies the fix did not move the bug.
proficiency_rubric.5: Handles intermittent, multi-component failures and improves the process so the class of bug is caught earlier.

label: Estimation and Sanity Checks
description: Order-of-magnitude estimates, checking units and ranges, testing a result against a simple case.

proficiency_rubric.1: Accepts a computed result without checking it.
proficiency_rubric.2: Checks units and whether a result is in a plausible range when prompted.
proficiency_rubric.3: Checks a result against a simple or extreme case unprompted.
proficiency_rubric.4: Estimates before calculating and uses the estimate to catch errors.
proficiency_rubric.5: Builds quick models to bound a design decision and states their assumptions.

label: Trade-off Reasoning
description: Weighing alternatives and naming what each one costs: area, speed, power, complexity, risk.

proficiency_rubric.1: Presents one solution with no alternatives.
proficiency_rubric.2: Mentions an alternative when asked.
proficiency_rubric.3: Offers an alternative unprompted and states one cost of each option.
proficiency_rubric.4: Compares options along the dimensions that matter for the stated goal and commits to one.
proficiency_rubric.5: Identifies the deciding constraint, quantifies where possible, and says what would change the decision.

label: Risk and Failure-Mode Awareness
description: Raising what could go wrong before being asked: corner cases, reset, invalid states, asynchronous inputs.

proficiency_rubric.1: Considers only the normal case.
proficiency_rubric.2: Handles a corner case when it is pointed out.
proficiency_rubric.3: Names the obvious corner cases unprompted (reset, empty, maximum value).
proficiency_rubric.4: Looks for failure modes systematically and says how each would be detected or prevented.
proficiency_rubric.5: Prioritizes risks by likelihood and cost and designs the verification around them.

label: Project Walkthrough
description: Explaining a project you worked on: the goal, your part, a decision you made and why, what was hard, what you would change.

proficiency_rubric.1: Lists what the project was without a clear personal role.
proficiency_rubric.2: Describes the goal and their own part clearly.
proficiency_rubric.3: Explains one technical decision with its reason and one difficulty with how it was solved.
proficiency_rubric.4: Answers deep follow-up questions on their part, and separates what they did from what the team did.
proficiency_rubric.5: Reflects on what they would do differently and ties it to a general lesson.

label: Ownership
description: Taking responsibility for an outcome, following a problem to its end, saying what you got wrong.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes problems as someone else's.
proficiency_rubric.2: Describes finishing an assigned task.
proficiency_rubric.3: Gives an example of following a problem past the boundary of their task.
proficiency_rubric.4: Describes a mistake of their own, its consequence, and what they changed afterwards.
proficiency_rubric.5: Shows a pattern of raising and closing issues early, with evidence.

label: Teamwork
description: Working with others: dividing work, handling disagreement, asking for and giving help.

proficiency_rubric.1: Describes working alone within a group.
proficiency_rubric.2: Describes dividing work and meeting their part.
proficiency_rubric.3: Gives an example of a disagreement and how it was resolved.
proficiency_rubric.4: Shows how they adapted to a teammate's way of working and what the team gained.
proficiency_rubric.5: Describes improving how the whole team worked, with a concrete result.

label: Learning from Mistakes
description: Describing a failure honestly, what was learned, and how behavior changed.

proficiency_rubric.1: Cannot name a mistake, or names one that is really a strength.
proficiency_rubric.2: Names a real mistake.
proficiency_rubric.3: Explains what caused it and what they learned.
proficiency_rubric.4: Shows a later situation where they acted differently because of it.
proficiency_rubric.5: Turns the lesson into a habit or a check that others adopted.

label: Structured Explanation
description: Explaining in an order a listener can follow: assumptions, approach, result, check.

proficiency_rubric.1: Statements arrive in the order they were thought of.
proficiency_rubric.2: The answer can be followed with effort.
proficiency_rubric.3: States the approach before the details and marks the result clearly.
proficiency_rubric.4: States assumptions first, structures the answer, and closes with a check.
proficiency_rubric.5: Adapts the structure and depth to the listener and summarizes precisely.
